done.why: I ran into the 300-turn limit while walking back toward the dam to get the sceptre and screwdriver. I had just spotted my lost scarab lying in the Troll Room. My score was 214 of 350 (it had been 220 before I died).

about: This is a treasure hunt under a white house. You collect valuables from caves, a temple, a flooded dam, a coal mine and a river, and bring them back to a trophy case in the living room. Most points come from solving small puzzles that each guard a treasure: a troll, an echoing room, a dam you can drain, evil spirits at the gates of Hades, a cyclops and a leaky boat. It also tests how you plan your load and your routes, because you can't carry much and some ways back are one-way.

moments.note: The trap door slammed shut and someone barred it behind me, so I suddenly had to find another way out.
I killed the troll in two blows. The fog that took his body away was a nice touch.
Typing 'take bar' in the Loud Room just echoed back 'bar bar ...'. 'echo' fixed the room's acoustics and I got the platinum bar.
'Your load is too heavy, the sword not least of it' kept stopping me. I spent a lot of turns juggling what to carry.
Bell, candles and book together drove the spirits from the gates of Hades. It felt dramatic, and I got the crystal skull.
Saying 'ulysses' scared the cyclops off, and he smashed a shortcut straight into the living room.
I found that the coal-mine slide drops you into the cellar. It was a great shortcut home.
Praying at the altar sent me up to the forest with the heavy gold coffin. That solved my problem of getting out.
Boarding the boat while carrying the sharp sceptre popped it. I hadn't realised the sceptre counted as sharp.
'fix boat with tube' only got the reply 'With a tube?'. It worked when I named the viscous material inside, which felt fiddly.
At the falls I had no sceptre and couldn't go back upstream. I tried to steer west and died going over Aragain Falls, losing my emerald and scarab.
The death message was funny and actually useful: valuables had 'rolled into some dark corner' and 'somebody tidy has put the lamp back in the living room'.
Praying at the altar as a spirit brought me back to life in the woods.
My lost scarab turned up in the Troll Room, just before the turn limit hit.

wished: I wished the boat warned me before I boarded with something sharp, or at least that the sceptre's description mentioned its point before it popped the boat.
I wished 'fix boat with tube' or 'put gunk on boat' worked without me having to name the 'viscous material'.
I wished the falls side had a way back, or a clearer hint that you need the sceptre before you go downriver.
I wished I could have reached the rainbow, the diamond machine and the thief's lair before running out of turns.
I wished I could carry more. Load limits took up a lot of my turns.

lines.line: The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
lines.why: It cut off my way back at once and set my main goal: find another route out.
A funny, clever clue that the room was eating my words.

lines.line: "Begone, fiends!" A heart-stopping scream fills the cavern, and the spirits, sensing a greater power, flee through the walls.
lines.why: This paid off the whole bell, book and candle chain, and it felt earned.

lines.line: The cyclops, hearing the name of his father's deadly nemesis, flees the room by knocking down the wall on the east of the room.
lines.why: One word solved a big obstacle and opened a route home.

lines.line: Oops! Something sharp seems to have slipped and punctured the boat.
lines.why: My most costly mistake. It cost me the sceptre for the rest of the river trip.
The game mocked me and I deserved it.

lines.line: anything of value has rolled into some dark corner in or under it, and somebody tidy has put the lamp back in the living room.
lines.why: After I died, this told me where my things had gone. It was funny and useful.

fun.why: Nearly every area had a puzzle that paid off well: the troll, the echo, the exorcism, the cyclops, the slide shortcut and praying with the coffin. The boat puncture and the death at the falls stung, but they made me laugh more than they annoyed me.

engagement.why: As a goal-seeker I had something to chase the whole time. Each score check showed progress (35, 110, 165, 220), and I always knew the next treasure I wanted.

difficulty.why: Most puzzles were fair and well signposted. The hard parts were the carrying limit, the sharp sceptre and the one-way falls area. They punished planning mistakes, not bad guesses, which felt fair even when it hurt.

interestingness.why: The map has satisfying links: the slide down to the cellar, the cyclops shortcut, the altar teleport and the two mirror rooms. The rules for death and coming back to life were a nice twist too.

prose.why: The writing is short and dry with good jokes ('Some moron punctured it', 'somebody tidy has put the lamp back'), and the big moments get vivid lines. A few replies were very bare, like 'With a tube?'.
